trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
Going left, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,1); going down, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes right.
Going up leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes right.
Going up would leave both cell (1,4) and cell (1,6) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going right leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes down.
Going right leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes left.
Going down, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes left.
The line must go down: left is number 7, which comes later.
Going right, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (5,4). So the line goes left.
Going left, the next 5 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at number 5. So the line goes down.

Going left would leave both cell (4,1) and cell (6,1) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going down, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,1). So the line goes right.
Going down, the next 4 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,1). So the line goes right.
Cell (4,4) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Going right, the next 4 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (1,5). So the line goes down.
Going right would leave both cell (4,6) and cell (6,6) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes down.
The line must go right: left is number 8, which comes later.
Cell (1,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Cell (2,2) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
